cars.generation: Original FF four-wheel-drive grand touring road family
cars.variant: FF Mark I — original English road brochure
cars.specification_market: Original Jensen Motors English two-page FF brochure, printed CGA/LB/966/2½M, hosted as 1966 by Auto-Brochures. Cover and full technical leaf PDF2 rendered and visually read at enlarged resolution. Selected Mark I road reference, not CV8 FF prototype, later FF II/III, ordinary rear-drive Interceptor, SP or modern restomod. Brochure does not give power or torque output; no magazine SAE/DIN figure is silently added. Museum technical accounts explain historical importance without making a universal first-in-the-world claim.
cars.summary: The Jensen FF brought Ferguson four-wheel drive and Dunlop Maxaret anti-skid braking together in a V8 grand tourer at an early stage of road-car adoption. Its mechanically controlled traction and braking systems make it an engineering landmark in the development of high-performance all-weather road cars.

cars.variant: 3.8 Sedan — US brochure four-speed manual with overdrive
cars.specification_market: Original Jaguar Cars Inc. New York US 3.8 Sedan brochure, hosted as 1964 by Jaguar Club Russia, four scanned pages. All pages rendered; full specification PDF2 and body/gearbox context PDF3–4 visually read. The 1964 reference follows host attribution, not an independently authenticated print date. Selected four-speed manual with overdrive; Borg-Warner automatic column excluded. Native 225 bhp at 5500 rpm retained without relabelling as SAE net or converting to kW. Heritage Trust’s 220-bhp narrative is history, not the selected US rating. Not 2.4/3.4, later 240/340, Daimler V8 or modified racing car.
cars.summary: The Jaguar Mark II 3.8 established a lasting sporting-saloon identity by combining XK six-cylinder performance with four-door accommodation. Its international touring-car and rally record, together with its enduring association with fast police and getaway cars, makes it a defining performance icon beyond Jaguar’s two-seat sports cars.

cars.generation: Original Bristol-engined Ace open road sports family
cars.variant: Ace Bristol — 1963 base production recognition reference
cars.specification_market: Original AC Cars/RAC production recognition application KJ2, FIA117 GT, cover marked year1963; ten-page PDF. Contact sheet and base cover/engine/transmission/chassis pages1/3/5/6 plus options page8 individually read. Base form covers Bristol engine prefixes B/C/D/BS and alternative compression/ratios; no single unverified output, compression ratio or D2-specific rating is invented. Selected base road car without optional overdrive, competition fuel tank, duplicate fuel pump or later anti-roll-bar extension. Club archive supplies chassis/body history. Not AC-engined Ace, Ford 2.6 Ruddspeed, Aceca coupe, Cobra, new carbon-bodied Classic or replica.
cars.summary: The Ace Bristol combined John Tojeiro’s lightweight tubular sports-car architecture and aluminium body with Bristol six-cylinder power, establishing an influential British road-and-competition sports-car family. Its independent suspension and the Ace lineage’s role in the development of the Cobra give it lasting significance beyond rarity alone.

cars.summary: The Sunbeam Tiger is an enduring Anglo-American performance icon, developed from the Alpine roadster with Ford V8 power and Carroll Shelby’s engineering involvement. Its compact production-roadster form and works motorsport programme give it a distinct place in the history of British sports cars with American muscle.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The Sunbeam Tiger is an enduring Anglo-American performance icon, developed from the Alpine roadster with Ford V8 power and Carroll Shelby’s engineering involvement. Its compact production-roadster form and works motorsport programme give it a distinct place in the history of British sports cars with American muscle.
